perspective:
From Carolyn Abebe’s subjective perspective, she has access to:

- She works with Marilyn Olson at a community bank; they are relatively new colleagues, and Carolyn sees their relationship as professionally respectful.
- During a busy week at the bank, Carolyn noticed Marilyn was unusually quiet and withdrawn, compared with Marilyn’s normally engaging demeanor.
- Carolyn asked Marilyn if everything was alright. Marilyn replied that she was overwhelmed with work and some personal stuff and thanked Carolyn for asking.
- In a later interaction, Marilyn responded curtly; Carolyn felt confused and slightly hurt by this.
- Carolyn told Marilyn she hoped she hadn’t overstepped, said she had had tough times too, and suggested talking can sometimes help. Marilyn replied that she appreciated it, apologized if she seemed off, and said it had been a hard week.
- After that, Marilyn appeared to respond positively; Carolyn felt relieved and hopeful about their budding friendship.
- Carolyn invited Marilyn to a small weekend get-together. Marilyn said it sounded lovely, thanked her, and said she would love to join.
- Despite friendly interactions outside work, Carolyn perceived Marilyn as still maintaining professional distance at the bank. Carolyn felt disappointed because of this.
- Carolyn directly raised their work dynamic, saying she felt a distance she couldn’t understand. Marilyn said she hadn’t realized it, apologized if it seemed that way, and agreed to talk about improving collaboration.
- After their private meeting, Carolyn believed they had cleared the air and better understood each other’s professional expectations and personal boundaries. She felt content and optimistic.
- Carolyn proposed teaming up with Marilyn on the new project proposal. Marilyn said that was a great idea, was glad they had talked, and looked forward to working more closely with Carolyn.
